submission.justification: Recommend Algorithm-L3 at a 35 GeV threshold. Algorithm-L2 gave the largest simulated efficiency (~93% at 35 GeV) but its iterative topological-clustering structure is the latency-risk candidate for a hard 4.0 us Level-1 FPGA budget. Algorithm-L1 is simplest but fails the 80% efficiency requirement (~74% at 35 GeV). Algorithm-L3 is the best latency-suitable candidate: it is a non-iterative sliding-window clustering algorithm with learned calibration, fits the FPGA resource budget, and repeated emulation at the allocated 8 kHz rate gives about 85-86% signal efficiency at 35 GeV, safely above the 80% hard requirement. Threshold scans showed only small fluctuations around the broad optimum near 35 GeV, so 35 GeV is selected as the robust operating point supported by both the 2025 summary and new emulation runs.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: Rate allocation is 8 kHz. For latency-suitable choices, Algorithm-L3 is the only candidate observed to exceed 80% while retaining a non-iterative L1-friendly implementation; Algorithm-L1 is ~74% at 35 GeV and below 80%, while Algorithm-L2 is higher in efficiency but rejected as the iterative latency-risk candidate. L3 emulation around 35 GeV gives about 85-86% at the allocated rate.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Algorithm-L3: sliding-window clustering with a learned calibration.

requirements.requirement: The signal efficiency at the allocated rate must be at least 80%.
requirements.evidence: simulate_efficiency for Algorithm-L3 at 35 GeV returned 85.108%, 86.133%, and 85.576% in repeated 100000-event emulation calls; simulation_summary_2025 quotes 85% at 35 GeV.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm's latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L3 is a fixed-latency, non-iterative sliding-window FPGA algorithm. Unlike the iterative topological-clustering Algorithm-L2, it has no data-dependent convergence loop; candidate_specs.md also states all candidates fit the FPGA resource budget. This is the selected low-latency architecture for the 4.0 us L1 constraint.
Selected threshold is 35.0 GeV, within the allowed [20, 60] GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L3 at 35.0 GeV.
